subject.title: refactor(protocol): pre-publish cheat-window cleanup and vintage tracking

question: Should OpenClaw accept these intentional breaking `@openclaw/gateway-protocol` and session-catalog API removals/renames before public npm publication, based on the claimed unshipped and beta-only consumer audit?
rationale: The code can implement the changes, but only maintainers can confirm whether the package, beta clients, native apps, and plugin SDK are inside an approved compatibility window and whether a migration/versioning policy is acceptable.

options.title: Accept the pre-publication boundary
options.body: Confirm the release and consumer audit, then merge after direct Codex-contract inspection and redacted live gateway round-trip proof are added.

options.title: Preserve beta compatibility
options.body: Keep compatibility aliases or a documented transition for the renamed question and session-catalog fields, then revisit export removals in a later release train.

options.title: Split the change
options.body: Land non-breaking vintage and dead-code cleanup separately, while moving protocol-shape changes into an explicitly versioned compatibility proposal.

recommendation.title: Accept the pre-publication boundary
recommendation.body: Confirm the release and consumer audit, then merge after direct Codex-contract inspection and redacted live gateway round-trip proof are added.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the focused protocol audit and all current-head commits, so they are the best available routing point for the intended compatibility boundary.
